partners.mechanism_chain: TF (HGNC:11773) —PRODUCES→ Transferrin (CHEBI:17684); Transferrin (CHEBI:17684) —DISRUPTS→ Iron transport into cells (GO:0015904); Iron transport into cells (GO:0015904) —LEADS_TO→ Anemia (HP:0001873); SLC18A3 (HGNC:11774) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicular transport of neurotransmitters (GO:0048480); Vesicular transport of neurotransmitters (GO:0048480) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Mutations in TF lead to insufficient transferrin, impairing iron transport and causing anemia (Atransferrinemia). Mutations in SLC18A3 disrupt the vesicular transport of neurotransmitters, leading to muscle weakness (Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome 21). partners.mechanism_chain: TF (HGNC:11772) —DECREASES→ transferrin (CHEBI:17609); transferrin (CHEBI:17609) —LEADS_TO→ Iron deficiency anemia (HP:0001892); APOB (HGNC:707) —DECREASES→ Apolipoprotein B (UniProt:P02607); Apolipoprotein B (UniProt:P02607) —DISRUPTS→ Lipoprotein metabolism (GO:0006869); Lipoprotein metabolism (GO:0006869) —LEADS_TO→ Abetalipoproteinemia (HP:0003279). Loss-of-function mutations in TF lead to impaired transferrin production and thus iron deficiency anemia. Loss-of-function mutations in APOB lead to impaired apolipoprotein B production, disrupting lipoprotein metabolism and causing abetalipoproteinemia. partners.mechanism_chain: TF (HGNC:11771) —PRODUCES→ Transferrin (CHEBI:17680); Transferrin (CHEBI:17680) —DISRUPTS→ Iron transport and homeostasis (GO:0006875); Iron transport and homeostasis (GO:0006875) —LEADS_TO→ Anemia (HP:0001903); Iron transport and homeostasis (GO:0006875) —DECREASES→ Erythropoiesis (GO:0000278); AVPR2 (HGNC:921) —DISRUPTS→ Vasopressin signaling pathway (GO:0007214); Vasopressin signaling pathway (GO:0007214) —LEADS_TO→ Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (HP:0000779); Erythropoiesis (GO:0000278) —LEADS_TO→ Anemia (HP:0001903). Loss-of-function mutations in TF lead to a lack of functional transferrin, severely impairing iron transport and thus disrupting iron homeostasis. This directly impacts erythropoiesis, leading to anemia. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in AVPR2 disrupt the vasopressin signaling pathway in the kidneys, resulting in nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Both diseases, despite originating from different genes, converge on the disruption of fundamental cellular processes essential for organismal homeostasis and survival, namely iron homeostasis and kidney water balance, which indirectly impacts erythropoiesis through severe anemia.

raw.translational: Understanding the shared disruption of essential homeostatic pathways, even with distinct genetic origins, can inform therapeutic strategies. For atransferrinemia, this highlights the critical role of iron delivery for erythropoiesis. For nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, it underscores the importance of precise hormonal signaling in renal function. Identifying commonalities in downstream effects or compensatory mechanisms could offer novel therapeutic targets for managing severe anemia or fluid-electrolyte imbalances in related conditions.
